reference_sql:
WITH lines_per_order AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_orders
FROM lines_per_order
WHERE n_lines >= 3
alternatives: WITH big_orders AS (SELECT order_id FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM big_orders
WITH lines_per_order AS (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n_lines >= 3) AS n_orders FROM lines_per_order

other_way.sql: WITH big_orders AS (SELECT order_id FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM big_orders
other_way.tradeoff: HAVING keeps only the orders you want inside the step, but the step then hides the line counts of the others.
